To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) CPF did not activate cholinoceptive areas, and 2) CPF elicited c-Fos expression in cytokines-related regions.
CPF-induced c-fOS expression is observed in cytokine-related brain areas, and not in cholinoceptive areas.
CPF induces a transient activation of c-fos expression, which is not associated with a significant cholinergic impairment in brain regions related with learning, memory and locomotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuroanatomical basis of the neurobehavioral effects of acute CPF intoxication.
the identification of the neuroanatomical areas that are involved in the acute neurobehavioral effects of CPF.
the identification of the neuroanatomical substrates involved in the CPF neurobehavioral toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuroanatomical effects of acute CPF intoxication are not related to the inhibition of cholinesterase activity.

the neurobehavioral effects induced by CPF may be related to the activation of cytokine-related brain areas, and that these effects are mediated through the activation of adaptive neural processes re-establishing choline tone.
the brain systems involved by CPF-induced neurobehavioral toxicity are not restricted to the classical cholinergic ones, but also involve cytokine-mediated systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neurobehavioral deficits elicited by CPF could be due to the disruption of the neuroendocrine-immune axis.
CPF-induced c-fus expression in the cytokine-related areas could be involved in the anxiety-like responses reported in CPF-treated animals.
CPF-induced c-fOS expression in cytokine related areas could be related to the development of emotional disorders in organophosphates-exposed organisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CPF induces c-fos expression, but not in the expected brain areas, suggesting that the neurobehavioral effects of CPF are not mediated by the activation of the cholinergic system.

the lack of c-fos immunoreactivity in cholinoceptive areas and the c-fos expression found in cytokine-related regions suggest that the neurobehavioral deficits developed in CPF-exposured organisms may not be related to cholinergic system impairment, but to other neurochemical mechanisms, including cytokines, involved in anxiety-like behavior and psychiatric stress syndrome.
the neurobehavioral effects induced by CPF are not related to the direct action of this pesticide on the cholinergic system.
